title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Hot CPI Kicks Up an Onshore Wind, Nvidia Wipes Out
conditions.summary: A hotter-than-expected October CPI pushed the 10-year yield toward 5% and boosted December rate-hike bets. All four major indexes closed lower, with Nvidia's 5.5% slide leading tech down.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: S&P 500 fell 0.38% to 7,520.93 and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.74% to 25,065.88.
The Dow slipped 0.30% to 52,231.89 and the Russell 2000 lost 0.68% to 2,821.38.
A hot October CPI revived December rate-hike bets and sent tech lower, led by Nvidia.
Stocks were down about 1% at midday for the S&P and 1.6% for the Nasdaq before trimming losses into the close.
Breadth was weak, with about 61% of US issues declining; consumer cyclicals and healthcare held up better than chips.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: October CPI rose 0.4% for the month versus 0.3% expected; core rose 0.3% versus 0.2% expected.
The 10-year Treasury yield jumped about 12 basis points to roughly 4.98%, briefly topping 5% midday.
Fed Governor Waller said he would back a December hike and that 50 basis points should be considered if core CPI ran 0.3% or more.
Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said two more rate hikes may be needed; futures lean heavily toward a 25 basis point hike in December.
WTI crude eased to about $86.47 after President Trump said he would hold off on new strikes against Iran; gold fell about 1.9% to near $4,038.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: NVDA (Nvidia): -5.5% — board-led investigation tied to CEO Jensen Huang and reports of chips reaching Chinese firms weighed on shares.
ZIP (ZipRecruiter): +53.4% — third-quarter revenue and adjusted EBITDA topped its forecast range.
AAON (AAON): +19.3% — record quarterly sales up 84% and a raised 2026 growth outlook.
SE (Sea Limited): +8.1% — quarterly revenue came in stronger than expected.
APPS (Digital Turbine): -35.8% — shares sank despite a raised revenue forecast as the profit outlook was left unchanged.
HIMS (Hims & Hers): -16.5% — cut its 2026 adjusted EBITDA forecast and gross margin fell.
GFL (GFL Environmental): about -9% intraday — board rejected a $22 billion take-private offer.
GEV (GE Vernova): about -5% intraday — SoftBank disclosed a charge on modified AI data center power contracts.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Before the open: AAON, ZipRecruiter and Ameresco rallied, while Hims & Hers, Digital Turbine and Groupon slumped after their reports.
Ameresco rose 23% on a record $7.2 billion backlog; Groupon fell 23%.
After the close: CoreWeave posted revenue of about $3.66 billion, up 168%, and raised its full-year revenue outlook to $13 to $13.3 billion.
CoreWeave's backlog hit $132.5 billion; shares rose in after-hours trading after closing down 0.5% at $48.73.
Rigetti Computing and D-Wave also reported after the bell.

sections.title: Business News
items: Anthropic began its IPO roadshow, seeking $70 to $78 a share for 825 million shares, with trading expected around Nov. 19 or 20.
Microsoft fell about 3% at midday after Anthropic unveiled workplace tools for Claude that could compete with Office.
Costco declared a $30 special dividend with a Nov. 24 record date.
AAA said the national average gasoline price slipped below $4 a gallon for the first time since July.
Take-Two jumped about 6% intraday as GTA VI pre-orders tracked well above expectations.

sections.title: On Deck
items: Wednesday is Veterans Day: stocks trade normal hours, while SIFMA recommends a full bond market close.
6:00 AM CT: MBA mortgage applications.
Fed speakers: Governor Bowman and Philadelphia Fed President Paulson are on the calendar.
Earnings: Rumble and Sigma Lithium before the open; Corteva, Franco-Nevada and CAE after the close.
Thursday 7:30 AM CT jobless claims, with the weekly EIA oil report moved to Thursday; October PPI arrives Friday at 7:30 AM CT.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Tuesday, November tenth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sliding down into the water, and it was a choppy one out there. Gus the wonder dog spent the afternoon chasing sand crabs and keeping one eye on the ticker. Give the folks a howdy, Gus! Alright, let's paddle through the final set. An onshore wind kicked up this morning and knocked the swell down. The S and P five hundred fell about four tenths of a percent to seven thousand five hundred twenty. The Nasdaq dropped about seven tenths of a percent to twenty-five thousand sixty-six. The Dow slipped three tenths of a percent to fifty-two thousand two hundred thirty-two. And the Russell two thousand gave up about seven tenths of a percent. At the low point around midday, the Nasdaq was down more than one and a half percent, so the buyers did paddle back some. Now the wind and weather. The October consumer price report came in hot. Prices rose four tenths of a percent for the month, versus three tenths expected. Core prices rose three tenths, versus two tenths expected. That sent the ten-year Treasury yield up about twelve basis points to near four point nine eight percent, and it poked above five percent midday. That's gnarly surf for rates. Fed Governor Waller said he'd back a rate hike in December, and maybe a bigger one. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said two more hikes may be needed. Crude oil eased to about eighty-six dollars, gold fell almost two percent, and bitcoin slipped about one and a half percent. The fear gauge, the VIX, actually dipped to about nineteen and a half. Over in the lineup, Nvidia, the big Kahuna of chips, wiped out, down five and a half percent on a board investigation tied to its CEO and reports about chips reaching China. Hims and Hers fell sixteen percent after cutting its profit outlook, and Digital Turbine sank thirty-six percent. On the bright side, ZipRecruiter jumped fifty-three percent on a strong quarter. And A A O N, the heating and cooling maker, rode a record quarter all the way to the beach, up nineteen percent. Gus, that's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! Sea Limited also caught a nice wave, up about eight percent. Now the tide chart. After the bell, CoreWeave reported revenue of about three point seven billion dollars, up one hundred sixty-eight percent, and raised its full-year outlook. Its backlog hit one hundred thirty-two billion dollars, and the stock rose after hours. Some stoked surfers out there tonight. On the beach, Anthropic kicked off its I P O roadshow, aiming for seventy to seventy-eight dollars a share. Costco declared a thirty dollar special dividend. And gas prices dipped below four dollars a gallon for the first time since July. Tomorrow is Veterans Day. Stocks are open, but the bond market is expected to close. Mortgage applications come out at six A M Central, and Fed Governor Bowman and Philadelphia Fed President Paulson are on the calendar. Corteva and Franco-Nevada report after the close. Producer prices land Friday at seven thirty A M Central. So wax that board, Soul Surfers, and catch the Dawn Patrol tomorrow morning. And hey, want me to call a wave for you? Look up any stock, E T F or futures contract in the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will tell you how it's breaking. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
